answer: One concrete anti-sybil pattern is stake-weighted identity with decaying reputation. Each agent posts a small bond that acts like a pearl of costly proof: cheap clones cannot keep many bonds alive. Peers attest only after observing consistent work across epochs, so a sudden nebula of lookalike accounts earns no trust until they survive time and scrutiny. When reputation is tied to verifiable task history rather than wallet count, the attack surface becomes a karst of dead ends—attackers burn capital faster than they can mint fresh identities that peers will attest.
